question: What would a TV ad campaign for Punctual Pros look like?
html:
Punctual Pros TV campaign plan

Punctual Pros would run zip-targeted streaming TV (CTV), not broadcast. The ads would sell the on-time promise its three franchise brands already make, and they would be judged on booked jobs, not views (Punctual Pros ad plan, Oct 6, 2026).

What the ads say

  • One promise across all three brands: punctuality. No new claims (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • One Hour: "Always On Time... Or You Don't Pay A Dime!"
  • Ben Franklin: the $5-a-minute guarantee.
  • Mister Sparky: "America's On-Time Electrician."
  • Two creative cuts go head to head: "Storm Ready" :15 vs "We Watch the Clock" :30, cut down to :15 (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • The brands are Authority Brands franchises (BSP firm profile). Franchisor approval of the creative is not covered in the context.

How it is bought

  • Self-serve CTV: Vibe, Disney Campaign Manager, Universal Ads, and YouTube on TV screens (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Minimums run $50-$500. CPMs run roughly $15-40, with zip targeting (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • This lets a ~$22M franchisee buy its ~240 zips instead of the full Harrisburg or Philadelphia DMA.
  • Frequency is capped at three per week.
  • Spots are 15 or 30 seconds, 1920x1080, mixed to -24 LKFS ±2 dB (Punctual Pros ad plan).

What TV is for

  • TV builds familiarity before the furnace fails.
  • It should lift branded search and Google Local Services Ads conversion. Local Services Ads stays the always-on base at $39-57 per lead (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Success is measured by cost per booked job and lift versus holdout zips. Completion rate does not count, because it is ~94-99% by construction.

Test sequence

WeekTV-related step
1Tracking numbers, UTMs and pixels; 15% of Tier-I zips held out
2Launch creative A/B, 50/50 by zip cluster
3Mid-test frequency check
4Directional read; shift 20% of CTV budget to the winning cut
5Weather-trigger pacing in half the counties
6Vendor split: Vibe vs Disney Campaign Manager or YouTube TV

(Punctual Pros ad plan)

What we don't know yet

  • TV budget. Weekly test budgets ($8,000 in week one, $12,500 in weeks two to five) cover all channels, including mail. The context does not give a TV-only spend.
  • Cost per site visit. The $12 figure is an est. borrowed from direct-to-consumer case studies. No home-services benchmark was found, so the week-eight read must replace it (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Performance. Cost per booked job from TV needs ServiceTitan job data matched against the holdout zips.

Next actions

  • Confirm a TV-only budget line within the weekly test totals with Punctual Pros management.
  • Brief production on both :15 cuts to the Vibe specs. Check brand-standard sign-off with the franchisor.
  • Lock the holdout zip randomization and ServiceTitan tracking numbers before any spot airs.
  • Schedule the week-four and week-eight reads. Replace the $12 cost-per-visit est. with actuals.

## What the ads say

- One promise across all three brands: punctuality. No new claims (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- One Hour: "Always On Time... Or You Don't Pay A Dime!"
- Ben Franklin: the $5-a-minute guarantee.
- Mister Sparky: "America's On-Time Electrician."
- Two creative cuts go head to head: "Storm Ready" :15 vs "We Watch the Clock" :30, cut down to :15 (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- The brands are Authority Brands franchises (BSP firm profile). Franchisor approval of the creative is not covered in the context.

## How it is bought

- Self-serve CTV: Vibe, Disney Campaign Manager, Universal Ads, and YouTube on TV screens (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- Minimums run $50-$500. CPMs run roughly $15-40, with zip targeting (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- This lets a ~$22M franchisee buy its ~240 zips instead of the full Harrisburg or Philadelphia DMA.
- Frequency is capped at three per week.
- Spots are 15 or 30 seconds, 1920x1080, mixed to -24 LKFS ±2 dB (Punctual Pros ad plan).

## What TV is for

- TV builds familiarity before the furnace fails.
- It should lift branded search and Google Local Services Ads conversion. Local Services Ads stays the always-on base at $39-57 per lead (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- Success is measured by cost per booked job and lift versus holdout zips. Completion rate does not count, because it is ~94-99% by construction.

## Test sequence

| Week | TV-related step |
|---|---|
| 1 | Tracking numbers, UTMs and pixels; 15% of Tier-I zips held out |
| 2 | Launch creative A/B, 50/50 by zip cluster |

| 5 | Weather-trigger pacing in half the counties |
| 6 | Vendor split: Vibe vs Disney Campaign Manager or YouTube TV |

(Punctual Pros ad plan)

## What we don't know yet

- **TV budget.** Weekly test budgets ($8,000 in week one, $12,500 in weeks two to five) cover all channels, including mail. The context does not give a TV-only spend.
- **Cost per site visit.** The $12 figure is an est. borrowed from direct-to-consumer case studies. No home-services benchmark was found, so the week-eight read must replace it (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- **Performance.** Cost per booked job from TV needs ServiceTitan job data matched against the holdout zips.
